title: The Lord's Day
hint: Zechariah's prophecy about the last days
intro: Zechariah 14 is one of the most detailed prophecies concerning the Lord's day - the final conflict and the triumphant coming of the Messiah. The chapter describes dramatic cosmic and geographical changes.

items.title: Nations Gather Against Jerusalem
items.text: The Lord will gather all nations to fight against Jerusalem. The city will be captured, houses plundered, and women raped. Half the population will go into exile, but the rest will remain in the city.

items.title: The Lord Goes Out to Fight
items.text: Then the Lord will go out and fight against those nations as he fights on a day of battle.

items.title: He Stands on the Mount of Olives
items.text: On that day his feet will stand on the Mount of Olives, east of Jerusalem. The mountain will split in two from east to west, forming a great valley.

items.title: The Lord Comes with His Holy Ones
items.text: The Lord my God will come, and all the holy ones with him.

items.title: No Day or Night
items.text: On that day there will be no light; the shining stars will fade. It will be a unique day - known only to the Lord - without day or night. Toward evening it will become light.

items.title: Living Water from Jerusalem
items.text: On that day living water will flow out from Jerusalem - half toward the eastern sea and half toward the western sea. This will happen both in summer and winter.

items.title: The Lord Will Be King
items.text: The Lord will be king over all the earth. On that day the Lord will be one, and his name the only name.

items.title: Punishment of the Enemies
items.text: All who attacked Jerusalem will be struck with a plague: their flesh will rot while they stand on their feet, their eyes will rot in their sockets, and their tongues will rot in their mouths.

items.title: All Nations Will Worship
items.text: Every survivor from the nations that attacked Jerusalem will go up year after year to worship the King, the Lord of hosts, and to celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles.

items.title: Holy to the Lord
items.text: On that day it will be written on the bells of the horses: 'Holy to the Lord.' The pots in the house of the Lord will be like the bowls before the altar. Everything will be holy.

footer.title: Christ in Zechariah 14
footer.content: Jesus ascended to heaven from the Mount of Olives (Acts 1:9-12), and angels said he will return in the same way. Zechariah 14 describes exactly this - the Messiah coming in power and glory to establish his eternal kingdom.
